title: Restriction as pullback return and the finite residue compositum
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, $m\ge1$, $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, $X_{0,m}=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$, and $Y=X_{0,m}\times_{k_0}k$. Use the actual common-stage coefficient categories, constructible hearts and Weil sheaves of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], [def-weil-constructible-heart] and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and the integral-normalized pullback comparisons of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category]. Write $g_X$ for geometric $q$-Frobenius on $X$, $H$ for geometric $q$-Frobenius on $Y$, and $P=Lg_X^*$ on the constructible heart [def-weil-frobenius-detailed].

Let $g_m:X_{0,m}\to X_0$ be the finite projection and $\pi:Y\to X$ its geometric base change. For a constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F=(M,\theta)$ on $X_0$, form its actual $k_0$-Weil pullback $g_m^*\mathcal F$, with the induced structure on $\pi^*M$. Taking the distinguished-sheet return of this pullback yields, naturally in $\mathcal F$, the $k_m$-Weil sheaf
$$\operatorname{Res}_m\mathcal F=(M,\theta^{[m]}),\qquad
\theta^{[m]}=\theta\circ Lg_X^*\theta\circ\cdots\circ L(g_X^{m-1})^*\theta.$$
Here the carrier is identified with $M$ by $\pi j_0=\operatorname{id}_X$; all pullback comparisons are the specified ones. On morphisms restriction is the original carrier map. This defines an exact functor $\operatorname{Res}_m$ on constructible Weil hearts. The cyclic normalization of $\operatorname{Res}_m\mathcal F$, placing its carrier on every semilinear sheet coordinate, identity transitions on the first $m-1$ arrows and $\theta^{[m]}$ on the last, glues to a Weil sheaf naturally isomorphic to $g_m^*\mathcal F$. This comparison is before any direct image.

For every closed point $z\in X_{0,m}$ its image $x=g_m(z)$ is closed. Put $d=[\kappa(x):k_0]$, $R=[\kappa(z):k_0]$ and $f=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]$. The residue-field maps induced by $g_m$ and $X_{0,m}\to\operatorname{Spec}k_m$ identify $\kappa(z)$ with the field quotient of $\kappa(x)\otimes_{k_0}k_m$ specified by $z$, generated by the images of the two factors. They satisfy
$$R=\operatorname{lcm}(d,m),\qquad f=R/d=m/\gcd(d,m),\qquad
\#\kappa(z)=(\#\kappa(x))^f.$$
These assertions allow geometrically disconnected or empty $X_0$, nonlisse sheaves and nonsplit residue extensions.

proof.text: Apply constantExtensionRestriction_data to obtain an equivalence e, its actual restriction functor R, the specified restriction carrier/Weil formula, preservation of finite limits and colimits, and a natural isomorphism R followed by e.inverse to the actual projection inverse image. This is the pullback-return and exactness part of the argument, before any direct image.

Apply constantExtensionRestriction_normalization to e and its restriction specification. It gives the natural isomorphisms on all semilinear coordinates, the successor equations for adjacent coordinates, and the normalized ordered-return equation for G=R followed by e.inverse. This lemma applies to the chosen e without assuming that its full functor satisfies SheetSpec.

Package R, its restriction specification and exactness, G, its normalization and the inverse-image isomorphism as the displayed conjunction and existential statements. These are exactly the witnesses from the first two steps. For m=1 the successor equations are vacuous.

For closed z, [lem-kun-closed-point-field] gives finite-dimensional kappa(z) over finite k_m, hence a finite underlying set. The actual field embedding kappa(x) -> kappa(z) makes kappa(x) finite as well, and the same closed-point criterion makes x closed. Apply [lem-zl-finite-field-base-change-residue-surjective] to the actual base-change square and actual residue embeddings. Their compatibility follows by applying Spec to the maps, using naturality of canonical residue-field points, and the pullback projection identity. Thus the specified pushout map psi onto kappa(z) is surjective.

proof.text: Surjectivity of the specified tensor map psi gives the canonical first-isomorphism equivalence B/ker(psi) -> kappa(z), compatible with the quotient map. Transport the field property along this equivalence. The two factor images generate B as a ring by the commutative-ring pushout generation lemma; induction on ring closure (zero, one, sums, negatives, products) puts the image of every tensor element in the subfield generated by the two actual residue embeddings. Surjectivity makes that subfield all of kappa(z). In Lean this is pushout_field_generated, followed by RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective.

proof.text: Write $K=\kappa(z)$, $E=\kappa(x)$ and $F=k_m$, regarded as subfields through their residue maps. A basis of $F$ over $k_0$ identifies its finite underlying set with $k_0^{[F:k_0]}$; since $\#F=q^m$ and $q>1$, $[F:k_0]=m$. By [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius], the $q$-power automorphism $\sigma$ of $K$ has order $R=[K:k_0]$; its restrictions to $E$ and $F$ have orders $d$ and $m$. Thus $\sigma^R=1$ implies $d\mid R$ and $m\mid R$, hence $L=\operatorname{lcm}(d,m)\mid R$. Conversely $\sigma^L$ fixes $E$ and $F$ pointwise and hence fixes every sum of their products. By step 5 these are all of $K$, so $\sigma^L=1$ and $R\mid L$. Therefore $R=L$. The degree tower [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] gives $R=fd$. Since $d,m\ge1$, the integer identity $\operatorname{lcm}(d,m)\operatorname{gcd}(d,m)=dm$ gives $f=R/d=m/\operatorname{gcd}(d,m)$. Finally, coordinates in an $E$-basis of $K$ give a bijection of finite sets $K\simeq E^f$, proving $\#K=(\#E)^f$. No connectedness, lissity or splitting was used; when $X_0$ is empty the closed-point assertions are vacuous.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q55-b92bf17a3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Shape: one commit with no new nodes. The statement is unchanged. stmt_deps gains def-dl-a1-constant-extension-data, which defines the distinguished sheet and the fibre identification that step 1 uses. No SGA is cited, and there is no re-split note for this item. Source: Deligne Weil II (1.1.8), last sentence (the Frobenius at z is the n-th power of the one at y), and the paragraph after (1.1.10) on p.152 (X0⊗F as a disjoint union over Hom(F_q,F)); both read in the pdf, and the item states them precisely. Step 1: πH=g_Xπ, and πj_0=id because def-dl-a1 defines a=π∘sheet, so πh_i=g_X^i and the transitions are P^iθ. The last arrow comes from the sheet lemma's H^m j_0=j_0g_X^m, and lem-pod's associativity (ℓ invertible) matches the compositor parenthesizations. Step 2: T of lem-zl-cyclic-return gives θ^{[m]}. I re-checked the induction uθ^{[r+1]}=θ'^{[r+1]}P^{r+1}u. Exactness holds because the cyclic lemma detects exactness on carriers (at m=1 for the source and at m for the target), and Res_m does not change carriers. Step 3: S and r_i=a_0⋯a_{i-1} are exactly as the cyclic lemma states, and the sheet equivalence glues them; no direct image is used. Step 4: X_{0,m} is of finite type over k_0, and lem-kun-closed-point-field(a) applied twice shows that x is closed. lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field then gives κ(p)≅κ(z) compatibly with both factor maps. Step 5, a finite domain is a field, is genuinely elementary. Step 6: by the Mathlib leaf on Frobenius order, σ has order R on κ(z), d on κ(x) and m on k_m, so R=lcm(d,m); the tower-degree leaf gives f=m/gcd(d,m) and #K=#E^f. Cases tested: (d,m)=(1,m),(2,3),(2,4),(m,m); m=1; empty X0; the non-split tensor product in the (2,4) case. Searches for lcm, gcd(d,m) and the item id find no duplicate and no cycle; the sheet and cyclic lemmas are unsplit with no proof_deps. Accepted tool_uses: lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition, lem-kun-closed-point-field and lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field, all generic tools that the unit does not supply.
